subject: Eviction wave impacting dedicated GPU pool (US-West) — recovery plan & follow-up
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@edgeworks.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eviction wave impacting dedicated GPU pool (US-West) — recovery plan & follow-up

Hi Sophie —

I wanted to reach out immediately with an incident note: starting at ~15:40 PDT we observed an eviction wave in the US-West dedicated pool that significantly impacted request success rates and latency for your reserved capacity. Your traffic experienced increased errors and elevated tails for ~90 minutes before we routed traffic to warmed fallback nodes.

What we did so far:
- Identified correlated preemption signals tied to a bursty maintenance job that overlapped with our warmup window.
- Applied emergency routing to isolate affected nodes and shifted your capacity to unaffected warm standbys.
- Replayed and validated active KV cache priming for your model variants to restore pre-failure performance.

Immediate customer-facing impacts we saw: increased token errors and latency >5s tail for ~1.5 hours, approximately 18% reduction in sustained throughput during the window.

Next steps we are taking (high level):
1) Full collection of allocator logs and KV cache traces (attaching a tar of the logs for your SREs).
2) Postmortem draft and timeline (we will share a preliminary write-up within 72 hours).
3) Credit proposal and remediation commitments — ops & finance are looped.

Can we schedule a short sync tomorrow at 10am PT to walk through timelines and any immediate questions? If that time doesn't work, suggest alternatives and we'll accommodate.

I apologize for the disruption — we know this impacts your SLA expectations. We'll make sure to provide clear remediation and compensation options.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: eviction_wave_logs_uswest_20280626.tar.gz (log)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eviction wave impacting dedicated GPU pool (US-West) — recovery plan & follow-up

Aisha / Marissa —

Quick technical recap from infra: the short version — we had a maintenance orchestration job (host-level kernel upgrade) that inadvertently allowed preemption marks to be scheduled on nodes with active warm caches. Because the warmup window overlapped with the maintenance window and our fair-share windowing had a bug (race in the burst allocator), we saw a cascading eviction sequence (eviction ACK storms) which caused the scheduler to temporarily drop priority rebinds.

Key evidence (attached logs):
- allocator_eviction_trace.log: shows eviction heartbeats and requeue delays.
- kvcache_priming_gaps.log: shows missing prefix priming for several model shards.

Mitigation applied:
- Paused the orchestration job across US-West; forced drain of affected preemptible set and promoted standbys.
- Backfilled warm caches using prioritized priming (our backfill worker started at 16:02 PDT and reached >95% priming for customer shards by 17:18 PDT).
- Hotfix queued for allocator race (will deploy in staging in 12 hours, prod within 48 hours after validation).

Estimated impact window: 15:40 — 17:10 PDT (we saw residual tail improvements through 17:40).

I'll drop the raw traces into the shared drive. We should provide the customer a timeline and at least one proposed mitigation to prevent recurrence: either block maintenance during customer's warmup windows or guarantee live-migration of warm cache to standbys (engineering preference).

— Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: allocator_eviction_trace.log, kvcache_priming_gaps.log
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eviction wave impacting dedicated GPU pool (US-West) — recovery plan & follow-up

Thanks Ben — this aligns with what I saw in the telemetry. A couple of customer-ops points:

1) Credits & commercial remediation: recommend a provisional credit equal to 15% of June reserved capacity fees for EdgeWorks, pending final postmortem. I will work with finance to produce the CSV credit offer and include the calculation breakdown.
2) Customer comms: draft a concise post-incident note focused on timeline, root cause, mitigations, and a clear compensatory commitment. We should avoid engineering jargon in the customer-facing summary.
3) Follow-up ask: schedule a technical walkthrough with EdgeWorks SREs to share logs and discuss hardening. Suggest 30-45m.

I'll prepare the credit CSV and the high-level customer-facing postmortem draft and attach both to the shared drive by EOD tomorrow.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Sophie

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@edgeworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eviction wave impacting dedicated GPU pool (US-West) — recovery plan & follow-up

Sophie —

Thanks for the questions — summary & commitments below before tomorrow's sync:

1) Pinning model_version: short answer — pinning a single model_version would have reduced the number of active shard priming operations, which likely narrows the blast radius, but it would not have prevented the root allocator race. We'll cover concrete examples in the walkthrough (Ben will show traces where multiple shard priming exacerbated ACK storms).

2) Credit offer: Marissa has prepared a provisional 15% credit for June reserved capacity; the CSV and invoice mapping are attached (credit_offer_edgeworks_20280630.csv). Final credit will be applied after the postmortem sign-off.

3) Logs & readme: attachment and Drive link with a short README (index + recommended grep queries) are live here: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/postmortems/edgeworks-20280626 (we included an example query for the allocator_eviction_trace).

4) Postmortem draft: preliminary doc is attached (postmortem_draft_edgeworks_20280630.pdf). It contains timeline, root cause analysis, and planned mitigations: a) block maintenance during warmup windows, b) allocator race hotfix, c) improved telemetry to detect early ACK storms.

5) Meeting: Confirming calendar invite for Fri, 2028-06-29 10:00 PT (30m). Agenda: timeline overview, technical walk (Ben), commercial remediation (Marissa), Q&A. Dial-in and link included in calendar invite.

We appreciate your patience — we'll continue to drive the fixes so this does not repeat. I'll be on the call as well.

— Aisha
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
